correctness.rationale: For each petal both hub-to-leaf resistances appear N−2 times in the all-pairs sum; the leaf-to-leaf resistance appears once. Using the triangle denominator pq+pc+qc gives the claimed exact decomposition. At fixed p+q and c the numerator is fixed and the denominator is uniquely maximized at p=q. This rules out asymmetric optima directly, including designs with one missing spoke. With r=c/a and s=1+2r≥1 the local cost-normalized objective is 2(N−2)+t+[t(N−2)s+N(4−t)/s]/2. For t<4 minimization over s≥1 gives the stated radical if its stationary point is above 1, and otherwise s=1; for t≥4 the function is strictly increasing. At the threshold the minimum remains unique at s=1 with zero closing conductance. Positive petal spends then have the unique Cauchy–Schwarz equality z_i=B√G_i/S. Comparing the local costs at a positive minimizer shows strict increase up to the boundary. A fresh full-Laplacian check at m=3 with a subcritical, critical and supercritical price gave K=39.5404190161; conductance sensitivities divided by price equaled K/B on active edges, tied at the critical missing edge, and were strictly smaller for the supercritical edge.
residual_risks: The numerical example checks a finite mixed-support case only. The result relies on equal prices within each spoke pair and the shared hub; no arbitrary cactus or asymmetric-price claim is made.
